name: Pointers - Foundations
subject: C++
description: Learn pointers from the ground up.

lessons.title: What is a variable?
lessons.explanation: A variable is a named box in memory. `x` holds the value `5`. It has an address (where it lives) and a value (what's inside).
keyPoints: Every variable lives at an address
The visualizer shows this in the STACK region

bloom.question: What does `int x = 5;` do?
bloom.explanation: It creates a variable x and stores 5.

lessons.title: Getting an address
lessons.explanation: The `&` operator asks 'What is the address of this variable?' So `&x` means address of x.
keyPoints: `int* p` means p holds an address
The arrow shows what p points to

lessons.title: Dereference
lessons.explanation: `*p` means the value AT the address p holds. `*p = 10;` writes 10 into that address, changing x.
keyPoints: `*p` is the value at that address

lessons.title: Reading through a pointer
lessons.explanation: You can also READ through a pointer. `int y = *p;` copies the value at p's address into y.
keyPoints: `*p` on the right reads the value
`*p` on the left writes the value
y gets a COPY of x's value

lessons.title: Reassigning a pointer
lessons.explanation: A pointer can be re-pointed. First p points to a, then `p = &b;` makes it point to b.

lessons.title: Null pointers
lessons.explanation: `nullptr` means 'points to nothing'. Always initialize pointers either to an address or nullptr.
keyPoints: Dereferencing nullptr crashes (which is good - visible)

lessons.title: Putting it together
lessons.explanation: Read through pointer, compute, write back. This shows pointers let you work with variables indirectly.
keyPoints: The variable was modified through ptr
